1.overview: Moses addresses Israel in Moab after defeating Sihon and Og, recalls the LORD’s command to leave Horeb, and explains the appointment of tribal leaders and judges. He recounts Israel’s refusal to enter the land after the spies’ report, the LORD’s judgment on that generation, and the failed attack that leaves Israel at Kadesh.

sections.heading: Departure from Horeb and Appointed Leaders

2.overview: Moses recounts Israel’s journey past Seir, Moab, and Ammon, where the LORD forbids taking the lands given to Esau’s and Lot’s descendants and marks the passing of the wilderness generation. The LORD gives Sihon king of Heshbon and his land to Israel after Sihon refuses passage, and Israel defeats him while avoiding the forbidden territory of Ammon.

sections.heading: Moab, Ammon, and the Nations Before Them

3.overview: Moses recounts Israel’s defeat of Og, king of Bashan, and the division of the conquered territory among Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. He recalls commanding the eastern tribes to aid Israel’s campaign, commissioning Joshua, and asking the LORD to cross the Jordan, a request the LORD denies while directing Moses to view the land and strengthen Joshua.

sections.heading: Defeat of Og and Conquest of Bashan
Moses’ Request and the LORD’s Response

4.overview: Moses urges Israel to keep the LORD’s commandments, recalls the covenant and the LORD’s revelation at Horeb, and warns against making idols. He describes the consequences of apostasy and the hope of return, affirms that the LORD alone is God, sets apart three cities of refuge, and identifies the land and setting of his instruction.

sections.heading: Commandments and the Covenant at Horeb

5.overview: Moses recalls the covenant made with Israel at Horeb and restates the commandments given there. After Israel asks Moses to mediate because of the fire and God’s voice, the LORD directs him to teach the people and commands Israel to follow his ways in the land.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Instructions to Moses and Israel

6.overview: Moses instructs Israel to hear and keep the LORD’s commandments, declaring that the LORD is one and calling Israel to love him wholly and teach his words to their children. He warns Israel not to forget the LORD or follow other gods in the promised land, and directs parents to explain the commandments through the account of Israel’s deliverance from Egypt.

7.overview: Moses instructs Israel to destroy the nations in the land, avoid treaties and intermarriage, and remove their altars and idols. He grounds Israel’s status in the LORD’s love and covenant, promises blessing for obedience, and assures Israel that the LORD will drive out its enemies while warning against fear and idolatry.

sections.heading: Israel’s Election and the LORD’s Covenant
Blessings and the Removal of the Nations
Assurance of Victory and Warning Against Idols

8.overview: Moses recalls how the LORD humbled and tested Israel in the wilderness, sustained them, and led them toward the promised land. He warns Israel to keep the LORD’s commands, remember the source of its prosperity, and avoid idolatry, which would bring destruction.

9.overview: Moses warns Israel not to credit its righteousness for possessing the land, since the LORD drives out its wicked nations and keeps his promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He recounts Israel’s rebellion at Horeb and elsewhere, the making and destruction of the golden calf, and his intercession for Israel and Aaron, appealing to God’s covenant and reputation among the nations.

sections.heading: The LORD drives out the nations

10.overview: Moses recounts the replacement tablets and their placement in the ark, the Israelites’ journey and Aaron’s death, Levi’s duties, and the LORD’s decision not to destroy Israel. He calls Israel to love and serve the LORD, keep his commands, love the foreigner, and remember the LORD’s justice, choice of Israel, wonders, and growth from seventy people in Egypt.

11.overview: Moses recalls the LORD’s mighty acts for Israel and contrasts Egypt’s irrigation with the land of Canaan, which depends on rain and receives the LORD’s care. He sets out the blessings of obedience and the consequences of turning to other gods, commands Israel to proclaim blessing and curse on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, and urges the people to keep the LORD’s statutes and ordinances.

sections.heading: The LORD’s mighty acts for Israel
The land and the conditions of blessing
Remembering the commands and possessing the land

12.overview: Moses commands Israel to destroy Canaanite worship sites and bring offerings to the place the LORD chooses for His Name. He distinguishes ordinary meat from sacred offerings, forbids consuming blood, and warns Israel against adopting the nations’ worship practices or altering his commands.

13.overview: Moses warns Israel against prophets who promote worship of other gods and prescribes their execution, then addresses enticement to idolatry by a close relative or friend and prescribes communal stoning. He requires thorough investigation before a city that turns to other gods is destroyed, with its plunder burned, and links Israel’s obedience to the LORD’s mercy and compassion.

sections.heading: Enticement by a Relative or Friend
Cities That Turn to Other Gods

14.overview: Moses identifies Israel as the LORD’s holy, chosen people and gives rules for mourning and clean and unclean foods. He commands annual tithes for worship at the chosen place and a tithe every third year for the Levite, foreigner, fatherless, and widow.

sections.heading: Israel as the LORD’s chosen people

15.overview: Moses commands Israel to cancel debts every seventh year, lend generously to the poor, and release Hebrew servants after six years with provisions, recalling the LORD’s redemption of Israel from Egypt and promising blessing. He also requires Israel to set apart firstborn male livestock for the LORD, eat it yearly at the chosen place, and exclude defective animals from sacrifice and blood from food.

16.overview: Moses gives Israel instructions for Passover, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles, including their appointed place, offerings, and participation. He also commands the appointment of impartial judges and forbids Asherah poles and sacred pillars beside the LORD’s altar.

17.overview: The chapter forbids defective offerings and sets procedures for investigating and punishing idolatry, requiring multiple witnesses and the participation of the people. It directs difficult cases to the Levitical priests and judge, then limits a king’s power and requires him to keep and obey the law.

sections.heading: Limits and Duties of the King

18.overview: Moses specifies the Levites’ provisions and equal standing in service, and prohibits Israel from adopting the divination and occult practices of the nations. He recounts Israel’s request at Horeb for a prophet like himself, then states that God will hold hearers accountable and that a prophet whose prediction fails has not spoken for the LORD.

19.overview: The chapter establishes refuge cities for accidental manslayers, distinguishes them from intentional killers, and provides for three additional cities if Israel’s territory expands. It prohibits moving boundary markers and requires multiple witnesses, thorough investigation of false testimony, and punishment matching the harm intended.

20.overview: The chapter directs Israel’s priest and officers to encourage the army, excuse men with unfinished domestic commitments or fear, and appoint commanders. It distinguishes the treatment of distant cities from the nations of Canaan and limits the use of fruit trees during a siege.

sections.heading: Encouragement and exemptions for the army

21.overview: The chapter prescribes an atonement rite for an unsolved killing and rules for a captive woman taken as a wife, inheritance rights for a firstborn son, and a rebellious son. It also requires the burial that same day of anyone executed and hung on a tree, so the land is not defiled.

sections.heading: A Captive Woman Taken as a Wife
The Firstborn’s Rights and a Rebellious Son

22.overview: Moses gives laws concerning lost property and fallen animals, clothing, bird nests, house safety, mixed seeds and materials, and garment tassels. He sets out legal outcomes for accusations about a wife’s virginity, adultery, sexual encounters involving betrothed women, and a man’s marriage to his father’s wife.

23.overview: Moses sets rules for entry into the assembly of the LORD, distinguishing among excluded groups, Ammonites and Moabites, and Edomites and Egyptians. He gives laws for camp purity, protected fugitives, worship and lending, vows, and taking food from a neighbor’s field.

24.overview: Moses sets out laws concerning divorce and remarriage, a newly married man’s exemption from duty, security for debt, kidnapping, skin disease, lending, wages, and individual responsibility. He also commands justice for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, including leaving part of the harvest for them, recalling Israel’s slavery in Egypt as the basis for these laws.

25.overview: The chapter sets limits on flogging, protects an ox at work, establishes a brother’s duty to preserve a dead man’s name, prescribes punishment for a woman who intervenes in a fight, and requires honest weights and measures. It recalls Amalek’s attack on Israel’s stragglers and commands Israel to erase Amalek’s memory after receiving rest in the land.

sections.heading: A Brother’s Duty to Preserve a Name
Punishment for Intervening in a Fight

26.overview: Moses instructs Israel to bring firstfruits to the place the LORD chooses, recite the account of deliverance from Egypt, and rejoice in the land’s abundance. He prescribes the third-year tithe and its declaration, then describes Israel’s mutual commitment with the LORD and its status as His treasured, holy people.

27.overview: Moses and Israel’s elders direct the people to inscribe the law on plastered stones at Mount Ebal, build an uncut-stone altar, and offer sacrifices there. Moses and the Levitical priests declare Israel the LORD’s people, assign tribes to Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, and proclaim curses that the people affirm with “Amen.”

sections.heading: Law Stones and Altar at Mount Ebal

28.overview: Moses sets out blessings for Israel if the people obey the LORD, including prosperity, security, and a place above other nations. He then details curses for disobedience, escalating from disease and defeat to siege, famine, exile, scattering, and return to Egypt.

sections.heading: Exile, scattering, and return to Egypt

29.overview: Moses recalls the LORD’s signs in Egypt, provision in the wilderness, and victory over Sihon and Og as he presents the Moab covenant to Israel. He describes the covenant’s reach across generations, warns that turning to other gods brings the covenant curses and exile, and distinguishes the LORD’s secret things from what is revealed to Israel.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Deeds and the Covenant
The Land’s Desolation and Israel’s Exile

30.overview: Moses describes Israel’s return to the LORD and the LORD’s promise to gather the people from exile, restore them to the land, and bless them as they obey. He declares that the command is near and sets before Israel life and prosperity or death and disaster, calling heaven and earth as witnesses to the choice.

sections.heading: Life and death set before Israel

31.overview: Moses tells Israel that he will not cross the Jordan, assures them that the LORD goes before them, and charges Joshua to lead them; he gives the written law to the priests and elders and commands its public reading every seven years. At the Tent of Meeting, the LORD warns that Israel will turn to other gods and break the covenant, directs Moses to write a song as a witness, commissions Joshua, and Moses places the law beside the ark before reciting the song to Israel.

sections.heading: The Law Read Every Seven Years
The LORD Warns and Commissions Joshua
The Law Preserved and the Song Recited

32.overview: Moses’ song recounts the LORD’s faithful care for Israel, Israel’s abandonment of the LORD, and the judgment and eventual vindication that follow. After Moses and Joshua recite the song, the LORD directs Moses to Mount Nebo, where he will see Canaan but die without entering it.

sections.heading: The LORD’s faithfulness and care for Israel
Moses recites the song and receives his final command

33.overview: Moses blesses Israel before his death, recalling the LORD’s appearance from Sinai and declaring him king over Jeshurun as he pronounces blessings for Reuben, Judah, Levi, Benjamin, and Joseph. He blesses Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali, and Asher, then celebrates Israel’s security and salvation under the incomparable God of Jeshurun.

34.overview: The LORD shows Moses the promised land from Mount Nebo and tells him he will not enter it; Moses dies in Moab and is buried in an unknown grave. Israel mourns for Moses, Joshua takes up leadership, and the chapter describes Moses as an unmatched prophet in Israel.
